Subject: Delivery playbook request — S3 <> pgvector bridge

Hi team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We can confirm Acme AI wants to move forward with a constrained pilot to validate an S3-backed pgvector fallback for cold vectors. Before legal/commercials, procurement needs a short delivery playbook so our infra team can approve operational handoff.

High-level asks:
- A short runbook describing sync cadence, expected latencies for 1M vectors, and failure modes.
- Clear owner for reindexing flow and TTL policy.
- What parts of Redwood's runtime are required (e.g., prefix caching, routing policy) vs. partner S3 lifecycle responsibilities.

Attaching a one-pager from Acme with their compliance constraints (s3-pgvector-bridge-scope.pdf). Can you get a draft by EOD Wednesday PT? We want to present to our infra lead on Thursday.

Thanks,
James

Subject: Re: Delivery playbook request — S3 <> pgvector bridge

On Mon, Jun 7, 2027 at 9:12 AM James Turner <jturner@acme-ai.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo last week. We can confirm Acme AI wants to move forward with a constrained pilot ...

James — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a quick ops checklist (ops-checklist.xlsx) that maps responsibilities and a short draft runbook below.

Draft runbook summary (v0.1):
- Scope: initial pilot = 1M vectors, single region (us-west-2), 30-day retention on S3 cold tier.
- Ingestion: Redwood inference runtime will write vector metadata and dense vectors to pgvector primary store. When TTL policy hits, vectors are exported to S3 as compressed parquet and indexed with lightweight pointers in pgvector.
- Read path: primary lookups hit pgvector; miss -> call S3 read adapter, stream back vector to runtime, insert into runtime prefix cache for N requests.
- Expected latencies: pgvector hit ~ <10ms; S3 restore path (with small warm-up) ~ 60–200ms depending on parallelism and object size.
- Failure modes & mitigation: S3 read failures -> automatic retry/backoff and circuit-breaker to fall back to approximate embedding search (re-ranking) on smaller shard.
- Owners: Redwood runtime (connor_obrien) for routing/cache, Partner integration (vanessa_ortiz) for connector config, Commercial ops (marissa_cole) for billing and escalation.

Karthik — can you confirm the reindex cadence options we discussed (daily incremental vs weekly bulk) and whether the runtime supports chunked incremental reimports without downtime?

Connor O'Brien
Principal PM, Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, James Turner <jturner@acme-ai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Delivery playbook request — S3 <> pgvector bridge

Connor — copied the ops-level details into the attached service-config-snippets.txt and added the config knobs we recommend.

Key clarifications for Acme:
- Autoscaling target: prioritize 95th p50 token budget for restore-path to avoid cascading spikes. Default suggestion: 3x baseline workers for restore concurrency.
- Storage lifecycle: Redwood expects durable objects with consistent object keys; we recommend a per-customer prefix and object versioning enabled.
- Security: Server-side-encryption (SSE-KMS) required, with key rotation window documented.
- Monitoring: We will emit two new metrics to Acme's account scoped exporter: restored_vectors/sec and restore_latency_p50/95. These will be part of the SLA we can commit for the pilot (limited).

Attachment: service-config-snippets.txt (contains sample S3 key patterns, IAM policy snippet, and redwood restore adapter config).

Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Erin Shaw <erin@pinecone.io>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: James Turner <jturner@acme-ai.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Delivery playbook request — S3 <> pgvector bridge

Thanks all — quick technical note from Pinecone (cc'd for partner context):
- We can support pointer-based fallthrough to S3 via our import/export pipeline. For the latency numbers above, aim for object sizes under 64KB per vector blob to keep restore latency predictable.
- We suggest using batched restores (batch size 64) and ensuring HTTP keepalive to reduce TLS handshakes.
- We'll provide a small helper library to handle signed URL rotation and idempotent restore retries. Expect delivery of that lib by next Monday.

Operationally the plan looks sound. Marissa — for procurement/billing the requested pilot is straightforward; raise any contract exceptions and we can loop legal in.

Erin Shaw
Partner Engineering, Pinecone
erin@pinecone.io
